scope: Parts of the FEEDAP consumer-safety guidance that bear on what must be characterised: which material is tested, identity with the commercial product, identification of metabolites and residues, the purity exemption and the QPS exemption. Grounds the assistant only. Dose-response, exposure and MRL sections are not encoded.

guidance.title: Guidance on the assessment of the safety of feed additives for the consumer
guidance.author: EFSA FEEDAP Panel
guidance.citation: EFSA FEEDAP Panel (Rychen G et al.), 2017. Guidance on the assessment of the safety of feed additives for the consumer. EFSA Journal 2017;15(10):5022, 17 pp.
guidance.license: CC BY-ND 4.0 (open access; redistributed unmodified with citation)
guidance.title_check_phrase: Guidance on the assessment of the safety of feed additives for the consumer
guidance.page_numbering: guidance_page is the PDF page number.

entries.title: What the consumer-safety guidance covers
entries.requirement: Guidance on assessing consumer safety of feed additives: studies needed (Section 2), requirements by additive (Section 3), highest safe intake and exposure (Section 4), MRLs (Section 5). Safety is assessed by comparing consumer exposure to residues with the safe intake.
entries.quote: The safety for the consumer is assessed by comparing the exposure of the consumer to residues in food products to this safe intake
guidance_anchors: The safety for the consumer is assessed by comparing the exposure of the consumer to residues in food products to this safe intake

entries.title: Test the active substance; the fermentation product must be identical to the commercial one
entries.requirement: Consumer-safety studies use the active substance. If it is in a fermentation product, test the fermentation product, which must be identical to the commercial one. With several active components, assess each and consider interactions; for complex mixtures that cannot be fully identified or separated, assess the whole mixture.
entries.quote: studies necessary to assess consumer safety should be carried out with the active substance [...] The fermentation product tested must be identical to that to be used in the commercial product [...] For complex mixtures, especially when the components cannot be fully identified/separated, the whole mixture should be assessed
guidance_anchors: studies necessary to assess consumer safety should be carried out with the active substance
The fermentation product tested must be identical to that to be used in the commercial product
For complex mixtures, especially when the components cannot be fully identified/separated, the whole mixture should be assessed

entries.title: Published studies: evidence that the additive is identical
entries.requirement: When data come from publications, show that the additive used is identical to the one under application, or that conclusions still carry over. For fermentation additives this includes the production strain.
entries.quote: evidence must be provided that the additive used in these studies is identical to that under application [...] For additives produced by fermentation, this includes the production strain
guidance_anchors: evidence must be provided that the additive used in these studies is identical to that under application
For additives produced by fermentation, this includes the production strain

entries.title: Justify omissions and deviations
entries.requirement: Applicants must justify omitted data and any deviation from the guidance.
entries.quote: Applicants should justify the omission from the dossier of any data or any deviations from the requirements detailed in this guidance
guidance_anchors: Applicants should justify the omission from the dossier of any data or any deviations from the requirements detailed in this guidance

entries.title: Aims of ADME and residue studies
entries.requirement: Establish metabolic fate in laboratory and target animals; identify and quantify toxicologically relevant residues (parent and metabolites) in edible tissues and products and select the marker residue; establish kinetics of total and marker residues.
entries.quote: to identify and quantify residues (parent compound and metabolites) of toxicological relevance in edible tissues and products and select the marker residue when required
guidance_anchors: to identify and quantify residues (parent compound and metabolites) of toxicological relevance in edible tissues and products and select the marker residue when required

entries.title: Radiolabelled test substance: justification and characterisation
entries.requirement: Justify the choice and molecular position of the label and describe its specific activity, radiochemical purity and stability.
entries.quote: A justification of the choice and the molecular position of the label should be given, its specific (radio)activity, (radio)chemical purity and stability described
guidance_anchors: A justification of the choice and the molecular position of the label should be given, its specific (radio)activity, (radio)chemical purity and stability described

entries.title: Metabolite identification threshold
entries.requirement: Identify all metabolites at >= 5% of the administered dose or >= 10% of total radioactivity in the animal (whichever detects more) and give a metabolic scheme. Identification means exact structural determination.
entries.quote: Efforts should be made to identify all metabolites present at 5% or greater of the administered dose or 10% of total radioactivity in the animal [...] Identification refers to the exact structural determination of components
guidance_anchors: Efforts should be made to identify all metabolites present at 5% or greater of the administered dose or 10% of total radioactivity in the animal
Identification refers to the exact structural determination of components

entries.title: Marker residue
entries.requirement: The marker residue is the residue chosen for assay whose concentration has a known relationship to total residues. Select it and give marker-to-total ratios for edible tissues and products. Consider non-extractable residues.
entries.quote: The marker residue is the residue selected for assay whose concentration is in a known relationship to total residues in tissues and products [...] Consideration should also be given to the amount and nature of non-extractable residues in edible tissues/products
guidance_anchors: The marker residue is the residue selected for assay whose concentration is in a known relationship to total residues in tissues and products
Consideration should also be given to the amount and nature of non-extractable residues in edible tissues/products

entries.title: Marker residue study design
entries.requirement: Minimum administration period 28 days (animals for fattening: the 28 days before slaughter); marker residue concentration measured with a validated analytical method of sufficient sensitivity.
entries.quote: The minimum administration period of the additive should be 28 days [...] Measurements of the marker residue concentration (MRC) should use a validated analytical method with sufficient sensitivity
guidance_anchors: The minimum administration period of the additive should be 28 days
Measurements of the marker residue concentration (MRC) should use a validated analytical method with sufficient sensitivity

entries.title: Relevance of residues
entries.requirement: First approach: total residues from labelled active substance are toxicologically relevant. Second step: discount the fraction incorporated into endogenous compounds and metabolites with reduced toxicological relevance. Structural alerts may help identify relevant metabolites.
entries.quote: total residues measured in edible tissues and products from target animals administered the (radio)labelled active substance are considered of toxicological relevance [...] Identification of toxicologically relevant metabolites can make use of structural alerts
guidance_anchors: total residues measured in edible tissues and products from target animals administered the (radio)labelled active substance are considered of toxicological relevance
Identification of toxicologically relevant metabolites can make use of structural alerts

entries.title: No consumer-safety studies: no exposure, not absorbed, QPS microorganisms
entries.requirement: No studies are needed if target animals are not exposed (with analytical data showing the substance is not detectable in feed at feeding), if the substance is not significantly absorbed (not for additives with a measurable nanoparticle fraction), or for QPS microorganisms and, in specified cases, enzymes and amino acids from them.
entries.quote: Appropriate analytical data to determine that the active substance (or related substances) is not detectable in feed at the time of feeding should be provided [...] except additives with a measurable fraction of nanoparticles [...] microorganisms considered by EFSA to qualify for the qualified presumption of safety (QPS) approach to safety assessment
guidance_anchors: Appropriate analytical data to determine that the active substance (or related substances) is not detectable in feed at the time of feeding should be provided
except additives with a measurable fraction of nanoparticles
microorganisms considered by EFSA to qualify for the qualified presumption of safety (QPS) approach to safety assessment

entries.title: Microorganisms and fermentation products: basic toxicity set
entries.requirement: Provide genotoxicity/mutagenicity tests and a 90-day oral toxicity study. For xenobiotic substances, the basic set augmented as appropriate.
entries.quote: For microorganisms and fermentation products, a basic set of toxicity studies should be provided consisting of genotoxicity/mutagenicity tests and a subchronic (90-day) oral toxicity study
guidance_anchors: For microorganisms and fermentation products, a basic set of toxicity studies should be provided consisting of genotoxicity/mutagenicity tests and a subchronic (90-day) oral toxicity study

entries.title: Toxicological studies not required for highly purified non-xenobiotic chemicals
entries.requirement: Toxicological studies are not required for highly purified non-xenobiotic chemicals, as a guide < 1% unidentified material on a dry matter basis. Characterisation of the unidentified fraction therefore decides whether this exemption applies.
entries.quote: non-xenobiotic chemicals highly purified (as a guide < 1% of unidentified material on a dry matter basis)
guidance_anchors: non-xenobiotic chemicals highly purified (as a guide < 1% of unidentified material on a dry matter basis)
